classification.reason: The coach instructs the player that the first vector on the forehand must go out so that the shoulder can adduct through the ball with velocity.

problem.title_as_question: Why should you swing out on the forehand instead of moving directly towards the ball?
problem.definition: Moving the racket directly towards the ball on the forehand forward swing like a volley eliminates velocity, whereas swinging out on the first vector allows shoulder adduction through contact.

symptoms.description: The forehand lacks velocity and resembles a volley.
The racket moves directly towards the ball upon release instead of outward.

causes.statement: Releasing the racket directly towards the ball instead of directing the first vector outward prevents the shoulder from adducting through contact to create velocity.

angles.summary: Swinging out on the initial vector sets up the position required to adduct the shoulder powerfully through the ball.
Moving directly towards the ball is appropriate for a volley where high velocity is not intended, not for a groundstroke.

solutions.summary: Send the first vector of the racket outward so that you can then adduct the shoulder through the ball.
